quotes: The pedigree contains 188 individuals spanning six generations with 18 affected members. Autosomal dominant inheritance is present.

notes.statement: In the Pakistan Genome Resource (173,303 exomes and genomes), Koch et al. (2026) identified 2 individuals homozygous for LRRK2 loss-of-function variants: a 42-year-old with a splice donor variant (c.706+1G>T) and an eGFR of 68 ml/min, and a 25-year-old with chronic kidney disease (eGFR 14 ml/min) who was homozygous for a frameshift (Arg1639GlyfsTer15). Recall-by-genotype identified a 49-year-old woman homozygous for c.1418+1G>T whose eGFR of 51 ml/min was lower than that of all 13 of her heterozygous and noncarrier relatives who were recruited. The authors noted that heterozygous loss of function in LRRK2 had not been associated with any phenotype, including Parkinson disease.
quotes: Heterozygous pLoF of LRRK2 has not been associated with any phenotypes, including Parkinson’s disease. Two carriers of LRRK2 homLoF variants were identified in PGR: (1) a 42-year-old individual with a homozygous splice donor variant (Human Genome Variation Society (HGVS) coding sequence c.706+1G>T) and low eGFR of 68 ml min−1
a 25-year-old individual with chronic kidney disease (eGFR = 14 ml min−1) who was homozygous for a frameshift (Arg1639GlyfsTer15)
identified a 49-year-old female individual who was homozygous for a LRRK2 splice donor variant, c.1418+1G>T (Extended Data Fig. 11a)

notes.statement: Koch et al. (2026) stated that kidney dysfunction in people homozygous for LRRK2 loss-of-function variants supports the renal findings in LRRK2-knockout rodents and in preclinical studies of LRRK2 inhibitors. They recommended monitoring kidney function during long-term LRRK2 inhibition for Parkinson disease, while noting that the number of carriers was small.
quotes: Although the number of LRRK2 homLoF variant carriers is low in our study, the observation of kidney dysfunction in these individuals provides human data that support the adverse renal phenotypes observed in LRRK2-knockout rodent models
Kidney function should be monitored during long-term LRRK2 inhibition.

notes.statement: In a cross-sectional study of 490 Jewish patients with PD, Inzelberg et al. (2012) found that 79 (16.1%) carried the LRRK2 G2019S mutation. Non-skin cancer occurred in 18 (23%) carriers compared with 49 (12%) noncarriers (OR 2.18, 95% CI 1.19-3.99, p = 0.01).
quotes: Overall, 79/490 (16.1%) genotyped patients carried the G2019S mutation.
Eighteen (23%) carriers vs 49 (12%) noncarriers had a non-skin cancer (p = 0.01, odds ratio [OR] = 2.18, 95% confidence interval [CI] 1.19-3.99).

notes.statement: Among Ashkenazi Jewish PD patients, Inzelberg et al. (2012) found that LRRK2 G2019S carriers were more likely than noncarriers to have a concomitant non-skin cancer, with an age-adjusted odds ratio of 3.38 (95% CI 1.64-6.97, p = 0.0009).
quotes: The OR for LRRK2 mutation carriers adjusted for age was 3.38 (95% CI 1.64-6.97, p = 0.0009).
Ashkenazi Jewish patients with PD who harbor the G2019S LRRK2 mutation are more likely to have a concomitant non-skin cancer than noncarriers.

notes.statement: Aasly et al. (2012) measured CSF amyloid beta-42, total tau, and phosphorylated tau in 26 LRRK2 mutation carriers (18 asymptomatic, 8 with a PD-like phenotype) and compared them with striatal dopaminergic function on PET with FD, DTBZ, and MP tracers. Reduced CSF amyloid beta-42 and tau levels correlated with lower striatal dopaminergic function, with a significant association between amyloid beta-42 and FD uptake; among G2019S carriers, significant correlations were also observed for tau.
quotes: Reduced CSF Aβ42 and tau levels correlated with lower striatal dopaminergic function as determined by all 3 PET tracers, with a significant association between Aβ42 and FD uptake.
When cases were restricted to carriers of the G2019S mutation, the most common LRRK2 variant in our cohort, significant correlations were also observed for tau.

notes.statement: Aasly et al. (2012) concluded that the disposition of amyloid beta and tau is likely important in both LRRK2-related and sporadic PD, even in early phases of the disease, and that these proteins may be useful biomarkers.
quotes: The disposition of Aβ and tau is likely important in both LRRK2-related and sporadic PD, even during early phases of the disease.

notes.statement: Marras et al. (2011) found that tremor was more often a presenting feature among 25 individuals with LRRK2 G2019S-associated PD than among 84 with idiopathic PD; LRRK2-PD patients had better olfactory identification, higher Beck Depression Inventory scores, and worse color discrimination, but the phenotype was largely overlapping with idiopathic PD.
quotes: Tremor was more often a presenting feature among 25 individuals with LRRK2-associated PD than among 84 individuals with iPD.
Although tremor is a more common presenting feature of LRRK2-PD than iPD and some nonmotor features differed in degree, the phenotype is largely overlapping.

notes.statement: Marras et al. (2011) found postural or action tremor more common among 29 nonmanifesting G2019S carriers than among 53 noncarrier family members, suggesting it may represent an early sign. Nonparkinsonian family members had higher UPDRS motor scores, more constipation, and worse color discrimination than controls regardless of mutation status.
quotes: Postural or action tremor was more common among 29 nonmanifesting mutation carriers compared with 53 noncarriers within the families.
Nonparkinsonian family members had higher Unified Parkinson's Disease Rating Scale motor scores, more constipation, and worse color discrimination than controls, regardless of mutation status.
Postural or action tremor may represent an early sign.

notes.statement: Saunders-Pullman et al. (2011) used the University of Pennsylvania Smell Identification Test (UPSIT) to compare 31 PD patients carrying LRRK2 G2019S, 30 PD patients without the mutation, and 46 controls. Olfaction was impaired in the G2019S PD patients compared with controls, but less than in non-LRRK2 PD patients (difference = 6.13, p = 0.0012).
quotes: Olfaction was better among MC (PD-MC) than non-LRRK2 PD (PD-NC) (difference = 6.13, p = 0.0012).
Olfaction is impaired in LRRK2 G2019S-mutation related PD, although less overall than other PD.

notes.statement: Saunders-Pullman et al. (2011) found that 28 nonmanifesting LRRK2 G2019S carriers had lower mean olfactory scores than controls (difference = -3.518, p = 0.006). The impairment was present in only a subset of them, and the authors suggested that olfaction might be a marker for developing PD in this group.
quotes: 28 mutation carrier family members (nonmanifesting carriers [NMC])
impaired olfaction was increased overall in LRRK2 carriers both with and without PD, though the impairment was only present in a subset of NMCs.
olfaction is impaired in a subset of LRRK2 NMC, suggesting that olfaction may be a marker for development of PD in this group

notes.statement: Alcalay et al. (2010) screened 953 patients with early-onset Parkinson disease (onset at or before age 50) from 13 movement disorders centers. They found that 35 (3.6%) carried the LRRK2 G2019S mutation. G2019S carriers were more often of Jewish ancestry: 17 of 31 carriers with a G2019S mutation alone were Jewish, compared with 12% of noncarriers.
quotes: One hundred fifty-eight (16.6%) participants had mutations, including 64 (6.7%) PRKN, 35 (3.6%) LRRK2 G2019S, 64 (6.7%) GBA, and 1 (0.2%) DJ1.
The association was driven by LRRK2 G2019S carriers and GBA N370S carriers who were more likely to be Jewish than non-Jewish (Table 4).

notes.statement: Alcalay et al. (2010) had data on grandparents' country of origin for 11 of the 15 G2019S carriers who did not report Jewish ancestry. Of these, 4 reported Southern European descent, 4 mixed European descent, 1 Eastern European ancestry and 2 Puerto Rican ancestry.
quotes: Of the 15 G2019S carriers who did not report Jewish ancestry, data on grandparents’ country of origin was available on 11. Four reported Southern European decent (Italy or Portugal) and 4 reported mixed European decent
One reported Eastern European ancestry (Russia and Latvia) and two carriers reported Puerto-Rican ancestry.

notes.statement: Alcalay et al. (2010) found that early-onset PD patients carrying LRRK2 G2019S were more likely than noncarriers to have the postural instability and gait difficulty (PIGD) motor phenotype (96% vs 58%).
quotes: LRRK2 G2019S carriers were more likely to manifest the PIGD motor phenotype, and GBA L444P carriers had higher scores on the UPDRS-III

notes.statement: Alcalay et al. (2010) found that PRKN carriers were more likely than LRRK2 carriers to report a family history of PD, even though LRRK2 disease is autosomal dominant. They suggested this might partly reflect incomplete penetrance of the G2019S mutation.
quotes: PRKN carriers were more likely to report a FHPD than LRRK2 carriers, despite the fact that LRRK2 is autosomal dominant and PRKN is considered a recessive disorder.
LRRK2 siblings may develop the disease at a later age) and by incomplete penetrance of the G2019S mutation.

notes.statement: Alcalay et al. (2010) concluded that penetrance remains unknown for these PD mutations. They stated that there is little or no role at present for genetic testing for PD in family planning or in predictive or prenatal testing, but that patients with early-onset PD who are of Jewish or Hispanic ancestry, have onset at or before age 30, or have an affected first-degree relative may benefit from genetic counseling.
quotes: Therefore, there is little or no role for genetic testing for PD in family planning, predictive, or prenatal testing at this time.
In summary, EOPD individuals of Jewish or Hispanic ancestry, those with AAO ≤ 30, and those with a family history of PD in a first-degree relative may benefit from genetic counseling.

notes.statement: Tan et al. (2010) studied 13 SNPs at Parkinson disease GWAS-linked loci (PARK16, PARK8, PARK1, and BST1) in 2 case-control cohorts totaling 1,349 ethnic Chinese subjects. PARK8 and PARK1 SNPs were associated with an increased risk of PD, and PARK16 SNPs were associated with a decreased risk; BST1 was not associated.
quotes: We conducted an analysis of 13 SNPs associated with PD GWAS-linked loci in 2 case-control cohorts comprised of 1,349 ethnic Chinese subjects.

PARK16, PARK8, and PARK1 loci but not BST1 were found to be associated with PD. PARK16 SNPs were associated with a decreased risk while PARK1 and PARK8 SNPs were associated with an increased risk of PD.

notes.statement: In a pooled analysis of their Chinese cohorts and 2 Japanese replication cohorts (1,366 PD patients and 16,669 controls), Tan et al. (2010) found robust association with the PARK16, PARK8, and PARK1 loci and also BST1. The strength of association was similar in Chinese and Japanese subjects.
quotes: A pooled analysis of our Chinese cohorts and 2 Japanese replication cohorts involving 1,366 subjects with PD and 16,669 controls revealed robust association with these 3 loci and also BST1.
the strength of association is similar between Chinese and Japanese subjects

notes.statement: In a review, Dächsel and Farrer (2010) noted that genetic mutations predisposing to PD, including those in LRRK2, are diagnostically useful in early or atypical presentations. They added that both affected and asymptomatic LRRK2 carriers offer a chance to define the natural history of PD, including penetrance, motor and nonmotor features, and related biomarkers.
quotes: Genetic mutations that predispose PD are diagnostically useful in early or atypical presentations.

Both affected and asymptomatic LRRK2 carriers now provide the opportunity to define the natural history of PD. This includes the frequency, penetrance, and rate of motor symptoms, nonmotor comorbidities, and their associated biomarkers.

notes.statement: Alcalay et al. (2009) found that among 925 early-onset PD probands (onset before age 51), LRRK2 G2019S carriers had a lower tremor score and were more likely to have the postural instability and gait difficulty (PIGD) phenotype than noncarriers (92.3% vs 58.9%), an association that remained after adjustment for disease duration and Ashkenazi Jewish ancestry (odds ratio 17.7). Carriers did not differ from noncarriers in age at onset, disease duration, UPDRS-III, levodopa dose, or MMSE score.
quotes: Carriers had a lower tremor score (P = .03) and were more likely to have a PIGD phenotype (92.3% vs 58.9%; P = .003). The association of the G2019S mutation with PIGD phenotype remained after controlling for disease duration and Ashkenazi Jewish ancestry (odds ratio, 17.7; P < .001).
Carriers and non-carriers had similar AAO (range: 13–50 years), disease duration, age at examination, UPDRS-III and MMSE scores.

notes.statement: Alcalay et al. (2009) identified the LRRK2 G2019S mutation in 34 (3.7%) of 925 early-onset PD probands from 13 centers; no I2020T, R1441C, or Y1699C mutations were found. Carriers were more likely than noncarriers to be Ashkenazi Jewish (55.9% vs 11.9%) but were not more likely to have a first-degree relative with PD.
quotes: Thirty-four cases (3.7%) (14 previously reported) were G2019S carriers. No other mutations were found. Carriers were more likely to be Ashkenazi Jewish (55.9% vs 11.9%; P < .001)
Carriers were more likely to report AJ ancestry (55.9% vs. 11.9%, p<0.001), but not more likely to report a first-degree relative with PD than non-carriers.

notes.statement: Alcalay et al. (2009) found that the association between G2019S and the PIGD phenotype was present in both Ashkenazi Jewish and non-Ashkenazi probands analyzed separately, and that it was mainly seen in the shortest disease-duration tertile. Among carriers, nearly all had PIGD regardless of disease duration, whereas in noncarriers the PIGD prevalence rose with disease duration.
quotes: the association between PIGD and G2019S remained when analyses were performed in 81 AJ and 610 non-AJ separately (AJ: OR= 9.9; 95% CI: 1.8–53.0, p= 0.008. Non AJ: all G2019S carriers were PIGD. Fisher exact p-value=0.004)

among carriers of the G2019S mutation, all but two subjects, both in the lowest tertile, had the PIGD phenotype, so that the prevalence in the three duration tertiles was 81.8% (9/11), 100% (8/8), 100% (7/7).

notes.statement: In a genomewide association study and 2 replication studies totaling 2,011 Japanese patients with Parkinson disease and 18,381 controls, Satake et al. (2009) found a strong association at LRRK2 on 12q12 (P = 2.72 x 10(-8)). LRRK2 was a risk locus shared with populations of European ancestry. The authors concluded that loci for autosomal dominant parkinsonism are involved in typical PD.
quotes: We also detected strong associations at SNCA on 4q22 (P = 7.35 x 10(-17)) and LRRK2 on 12q12 (P = 2.72 x 10(-8)), both of which are implicated in autosomal dominant forms of parkinsonism.
we identified PARK16, SNCA and LRRK2 as shared risk loci for PD and BST1 and MAPT as loci showing population differences

notes.statement: Gan-Or et al. (2010) screened 600 Ashkenazi PD patients for LRRK2 G2019S and for 8 GBA mutations. More LRRK2 G2019S carriers reported muscle stiffness (rigidity, p = 0.007) and balance disturbances (p = 0.008) as initial symptoms, whereas more GBA mutation carriers reported slowness (bradykinesia, p = 0.021). The authors suggested that LRRK2 and GBA mutations have distinct effects on the initial symptoms of PD.
quotes: More LRRK2 G2019S carriers reported muscle stiffness (rigidity, p = 0.007) and balance disturbances (p = 0.008), while more GBA mutation carriers reported slowness (bradykinesia, p = 0.021).
These results suggest distinct effects of LRRK2 or GBA mutations on the initial symptoms of PD.

notes.statement: Lesage et al. (2009) sequenced all 51 coding exons of LRRK2 in index cases from 226 Parkinson disease families compatible with autosomal dominant inheritance, mostly from France (182) and North Africa (14). They found 8 potentially or proven pathogenic mutations in 22 probands (9.7%), most of them located in functional domains of the LRRK2 protein.
quotes: We performed extensive mutation analyses of all 51 coding exons of the LRRK2 gene in index cases from 226 Parkinson's disease families compatible with autosomal dominant inheritance, mostly from France (n = 182) and North Africa (n = 14).
Eight potentially or proven pathogenic mutations were found in 22 probands (9.7%).
Most potentially or proven pathogenic mutations were located in the functional domains of the Lrrk2 protein.

notes.statement: Lesage et al. (2009) found the LRRK2 G2019S mutation in 13 of 226 probands (5.8%) with autosomal dominant Parkinson disease. Six of these were from North Africa, which was 43% of the North African probands. They concluded that LRRK2 mutations are a common cause of autosomal dominant Parkinson disease in Europe and North Africa.
quotes: The common p.G2019S mutation was identified in 13 probands (5.8%) including six from North Africa (43%).
This study leads us to conclude that LRRK2 mutations are a common cause of autosomal dominant Parkinson's disease in Europe and North Africa.

notes.statement: Lesage et al. (2009) found 79 LRRK2 sequence variants, 29 of them novel. They considered 2 novel variants, H1216R and T1410M, probably not causative.
quotes: We found 79 sequence variants, 29 of which were novel.
two novel variants, p.H1216R and p.T1410M, that are probably not causative

notes.statement: Nandhagopal et al. (2008) performed multitracer PET in 13 members of the LRRK2 R1441C kindred family D and rescanned 5 of them 2 to 3 years later. In 2 mutation carriers and 1 genealogically at-risk subject, presynaptic dopaminergic PET markers declined significantly faster than the expected rate in healthy controls.
quotes: Thirteen family D subjects underwent PET scans of presynaptic dopaminergic integrity and five subjects were rescanned 2 to 3 years later.

In subjects 8, 9 (mutation carriers), and 13 (genealogically at risk subject), there was a decline in PET markers over the course of the study that was significantly greater than the expected rate of decline in healthy controls.

notes.statement: Nandhagopal et al. (2008) found that reduced dopamine transporter binding was the earliest sign of subclinical dopaminergic dysfunction in presymptomatic LRRK2 mutation carriers. Progression to clinical disease was generally associated with the appearance of abnormal fluorodopa uptake.
quotes: Reduced dopamine transporter binding was the earliest indication of subclinical dopaminergic dysfunction and progression to clinical disease was generally associated with the emergence of abnormal fluorodopa uptake.

notes.statement: Lesage et al. (2008) examined whether the common LRRK2 G2019S mutation is related to dyskinesias in North African patients with Parkinson disease.
quotes: Is the common LRRK2 G2019S mutation related to dyskinesias in North African Parkinson disease?

notes.statement: Silveira-Moriyama et al. (2008) found that odor identification (UPSIT) was reduced in 19 parkinsonian carriers of the LRRK2 G2019S mutation compared with healthy controls, to a degree similar to that in patients with PD. In contrast, 2 asymptomatic carriers had smell test results in the normal range.
quotes: The mean UPSIT score in G2019S parkinsonian carriers was lower than that in healthy controls (p < 0.001) and similar to that found in patients with PD (p > 0.999).
Smell tests in two asymptomatic carriers of the G2019S mutation were in the normal range.

notes.statement: Silveira-Moriyama et al. (2008) found alpha-synuclein accumulation with Lewy bodies in the rhinencephalon in all 4 parkinsonian G2019S LRRK2 carriers examined postmortem.
quotes: We found alpha-syn accumulation with Lewy bodies in the rhinencephalon in all four cases examined pathologically.

notes.statement: Choi et al. (2008) studied 72 unrelated Korean patients with early-onset Parkinson disease (onset at or before age 50). They found the LRRK2 G2385R variant in the heterozygous state in 9 patients (12.5%), and no patient carried the G2019S mutation.
quotes: Nine patients (12.5%) had heterozygous G2385R polymorphism of LRRK2, whereas none had G2019S mutation.

notes.statement: Choi et al. (2008) found variants in PARKIN, PINK1, LRRK2 and SNCA, which they considered causes or genetic risk factors, in 25% of Korean patients with early-onset Parkinson disease. PARKIN mutations were the most common genetic cause.
quotes: We identified genetic variants in PARKIN, PINK1, LRRK2, and SNCA as a cause or genetic risk factors for PD in 25% of Korean EOPD, and mutation of PARKIN was the most common genetic cause.

notes.statement: Liu et al. (2008) generated transgenic Drosophila expressing wild-type human LRRK2 or LRRK2-G2019S using the GAL4/UAS system. Expression of either form in photoreceptor cells caused retinal degeneration, and neuronal expression produced adult-onset selective loss of dopaminergic neurons, locomotor dysfunction, and early mortality. The G2019S mutant caused a more severe parkinsonism-like phenotype than equivalent levels of wild-type LRRK2.
quotes: Expression of either wild-type human LRRK2 or LRRK2-G2019S in the photoreceptor cells caused retinal degeneration.
Expression of LRRK2 or LRRK2-G2019S in neurons produced adult-onset selective loss of dopaminergic neurons, locomotor dysfunction, and early mortality.
Expression of mutant G2019S-LRRK2 caused a more severe parkinsonism-like phenotype than expression of equivalent levels of wild-type LRRK2.

notes.statement: In the Drosophila LRRK2-G2019S model, Liu et al. (2008) found that treatment with L-DOPA improved mutant LRRK2-induced locomotor impairment but did not prevent the loss of tyrosine hydroxylase-positive neurons. They stated that this was, to their knowledge, the first in vivo gain-of-function model recapitulating several key features of LRRK2-linked parkinsonism.
quotes: Treatment with l-DOPA improved mutant LRRK2-induced locomotor impairment but did not prevent the loss of tyrosine hydroxylase-positive neurons.
To our knowledge, this is the first in vivo"gain-of-function" model which recapitulates several key features of LRRK2-linked human parkinsonism.

notes.statement: Orr-Urtreger et al. (2007) screened Jewish Israeli patients with PD for LRRK2 mutations and found only G2019S. It was present in 14.8% of Ashkenazi and 2.7% of non-Ashkenazi patients, and in 26% of Ashkenazi familial cases and 10.6% of apparently sporadic cases. Carrier frequencies were 2.4% in Ashkenazi controls and 0.4% in non-Ashkenazi controls.
quotes: Only the G2019S mutation was identified among our patients with PD, 14.8% in the Ashkenazi and 2.7% in the non-Ashkenazi patients, and in 26% and 10.6% of the Ashkenazi familial and apparently sporadic cases.
The carrier frequencies in the Ashkenazi and non-Ashkenazi control samples were 2.4% and 0.4%.

notes.statement: Orr-Urtreger et al. (2007) typed 6 microsatellite markers spanning LRRK2. They found a common shared haplotype in all non-Ashkenazi and half-Ashkenazi G2019S carriers, and in all full-Ashkenazi carriers tested except 2.
quotes: A common shared haplotype was detected in all non-Ashkenazi and half-Ashkenazi carriers and in all full-Ashkenazi carriers tested, except two.

notes.statement: Orr-Urtreger et al. (2007) found that women and patients with a positive family history of PD were significantly over-represented among G2019S carriers. Age at onset was similar in carriers and noncarriers. They suggested that gender affects the frequency of the mutation among patients.
quotes: Women and patients with a positive family history of PD were significantly over-represented among the G2019S mutation carriers. Age at disease onset was similar in carriers and noncarriers.
gender affects its frequency among patients

notes.statement: Orr-Urtreger et al. (2007) concluded that testing symptomatic patients may help establish the diagnosis of PD. They considered the value of screening asymptomatic individuals questionable until the penetrance and age-dependent risk of G2019S are better known.
quotes: Although testing symptomatic patients may help establish the diagnosis of PD, the value of screening asymptomatic individuals remains questionable until the penetrance and age-dependent risk of this mutation are more accurately assessed

notes.statement: Chen-Plotkin et al. (2008) screened 434 individuals with a range of neurodegenerative diseases (254 clinic patients and 180 brain bank autopsy cases) for G2019S and other previously reported LRRK2 mutations. They found a mutation in 8 cases, 2 of whom presented with cognitive deficits and were diagnosed with corticobasal syndrome and primary progressive aphasia. The authors concluded that the clinical presentation of LRRK2-associated neurodegenerative disease may be more heterogeneous than previously thought.
quotes: A total of 254 patients recruited from neurodegenerative disease clinics and 180 neurodegenerative disease autopsy cases from the University of Pennsylvania brain bank were evaluated.
The clinical presentation of LRRK2-associated neurodegenerative disease may be more heterogeneous than previously assumed.

notes.statement: Rajput et al. (2006) suggested that alpha-synucleinopathy and tauopathy, the main pathologies associated with parkinsonism, may be alternate outcomes of the same underlying genetic cause, the LRRK2 G2019S mutation.
quotes: Thus alpha-synucleinopathy and tauopathy, the predominant pathologies associated with parkinsonism, may be alternate outcomes of the same underlying genetic cause.

notes.statement: Rajput et al. (2006) found no evidence that either tau or alpha-synuclein protein interacts directly with LRRK2.
quotes: Intriguingly, we observe no evidence of a direct interaction between either the tau or alpha-synuclein protein with Lrrk2.

notes.statement: Ishihara et al. (2006) found no observable differences between the phenotypes of Parkinson disease patients homozygous for the LRRK2 G2019S mutation and previously published heterozygous patients. They concluded that LRRK2-related Parkinson disease has typical clinical features, and that the similarity between homozygotes and heterozygotes does not support a gene dosage effect.
quotes: There were no observable differences between the homozygote and heterozygote phenotypes.
Parkinson disease related to LRRK2 is characterized by typical clinical features, and the similarities between patients with homozygous and heterozygous mutations do not support a gene dosage effect.

notes.statement: Zhu et al. (2006) reported that LRRK2 protein is a component of Lewy bodies.
quotes: LRRK2 protein is a component of Lewy bodies.

notes.statement: Giasson et al. (2006) found accumulations of Lrrk2 only in the patient with parkinsonism but no Lewy bodies. Lrrk2 was not detected in other types of pathological inclusions. The authors suggested that LRRK2 mutations may make select neuronal populations more vulnerable to cellular insults that can lead to aberrant protein aggregation.
quotes: Lrrk2 accumulations were unique to this patient and Lrrk2 was not detected in other types of pathological inclusions.
Lrrk2 mutations may prime select neuronal populations to cellular insults that can lead to aberrant protein aggregation

notes.statement: Using biochemical analysis, Giasson et al. (2006) showed that Lrrk2 is mainly a soluble cytoplasmic protein of about 250 kD. It was expressed throughout the brain and also in many other organs.
quotes: Biochemical analysis showed that Lrrk2 is predominantly a soluble approximately 250 kDa cytoplasmic protein expressed throughout the brain but also in many other organs.

notes.statement: Ross et al. (2006) found the LRRK2 G2019S mutation in about 2% (8 of 405) of autopsied Parkinson disease/Lewy body disease cases. They also found it in 1 control subject and 1 patient with Alzheimer disease, which they took to reflect reduced penetrance.
quotes: Lrrk2 G2019S was observed in approximately 2% (n = 8) of our Parkinson's disease/Lewy body disease cases (n = 405).
The mutation was also found in one control subject and one Alzheimer's disease patient, reflecting reduced penetrance.

notes.statement: Ross et al. (2006) reported that Lewy body disease was the most common neuropathology in Parkinson disease associated with LRRK2 G2019S.
quotes: Herein, we report that the most common neuropathology of G2019S-associated Parkinson's disease is Lewy body disease.

notes.statement: Ross et al. (2006) suggested that treatments aimed at modulating LRRK2 kinase activity may be important for patients with genetically defined familial Parkinson disease or typical sporadic Parkinson disease.
quotes: Therapeutic strategies targeted at modulating Lrrk2 kinase activity may be important to treat patients with genetically defined familial or typical sporadic Parkinson's disease.

notes.statement: Skipper et al. (2005) characterized linkage disequilibrium across LRRK2 using densely spaced SNPs and selected tagging SNPs; in an epidemiologically matched Chinese sporadic PD case-control series of 932 individuals, both single tSNP and haplotype analyses yielded significant evidence for association. One haplotype dramatically increased disease risk when present in 2 copies (OR = 5.5, 95% CI 2.1-14.0, P = 0.0001).
quotes: Both single tSNP and tSNP haplotype analyses, using a large epidemiologically matched sporadic case-control series comprising 932 individuals, yielded significant evidence for disease association.
We identified a haplotype that dramatically increases disease risk when present in two copies (OR=5.5, 95%CI=2.1-14.0, P=0.0001).
Thus, we provide the first evidence that common genetic variation within LRRK2 contributes to the risk of sporadic PD in the Chinese population.

notes.statement: Farrer et al. (2005) screened 786 Parkinson disease probands, 32 affected sibs, 1,044 unaffected sibs, and 278 unrelated controls for 9 LRRK2 mutations using allelic discrimination assays. They identified mutations in 6 probands, 1 affected sib, 1 unaffected sib, and 1 unrelated control, and concluded that LRRK2 mutations only rarely cause idiopathic PD.
quotes: the authors studied 786 PD probands, 32 affected siblings, 1,044 unaffected siblings, and 278 unrelated controls.
identified these in six probands with PD, one affected sibling, one unaffected sibling, and one unrelated control. Thus LRRK2 mutations only rarely cause idiopathic PD.

notes.statement: Paisán-Ruíz et al. (2005) sequenced all 51 LRRK2 coding exons in 23 probands of families with dominantly inherited PD and identified heterozygous mutations in 3: 2 had G2019S and 1 had a novel I1371V substitution; mutation frequencies were evaluated in 180 neurologically normal controls.
quotes: All 51 LRRK2 coding exons were sequenced in 23 probands and the mutation frequencies were evaluated in 180 neurologically normal control subjects.

notes.statement: In a case-control study of 121 PD patients (predominantly white Canadians, 84% with onset before age 50) and 250 controls, Paisán-Ruíz et al. (2005) found no association between PD and 4 common coding LRRK2 polymorphisms, and no modifying effect of these genotypes or APOE genotypes on age at onset, although a modest risk effect could not be excluded.
quotes: there was no association between PD and any of the four polymorphisms at the allelic or genotypic levels (p > 0.17).
the authors did not detect a modifying effect for any genotype or of APOE genotypes upon the age at onset in the PD group (p > 0.20).

notes.statement: Lesage et al. (2005) carried out LRRK2 haplotype analyses in European and North African families with Parkinson disease. They reported a common founder for the G2019S mutation, dating from the 13th century.
quotes: LRRK2 haplotype analyses in European and North African families with Parkinson disease: a common founder for the G2019S mutation dating from the 13th century.

notes.statement: Funayama et al. (2005) did not detect the Sagamihara family LRRK2 mutation or other known LRRK2 mutations in Japanese patients with sporadic Parkinson disease.
quotes: We did not detect this mutation or other known mutations of the LRRK2 gene in Japanese patients with sporadic Parkinson's disease.

notes.statement: In 4 Basque families with autosomal dominant Parkinson disease, Paisàn-Ruìz et al. (2005) found evidence for linkage to the PARK8 locus. The maximum 2-point lod score was 3.21 (theta = 0.00) at marker D12S345.
quotes: We genetically characterized four Basque families and found evidence for linkage of autosomal dominant PD to the PARK8 locus, with a maximum 2-point logarithm of odds score of 3.21 (theta = 0.00) for marker D12S345.

notes.statement: Gilks et al. (2005) sequenced exon 41 of LRRK2 in 482 patients with idiopathic Parkinson disease, 263 of whom had pathologically confirmed disease, and found the heterozygous G2019S mutation in 8 (1.6%). They concluded that a common single Mendelian mutation is implicated in sporadic Parkinson disease.
quotes: We assessed 482 patients with the disorder, of whom 263 had pathologically confirmed disease, by direct sequencing for mutations in exon 41 of LRRK2. The mutation was present in eight (1.6%) patients.
We have shown that a common single Mendelian mutation is implicated in sporadic Parkinson's disease.

notes.statement: Gilks et al. (2005) suggested that testing for the LRRK2 G2019S mutation would be important in the management and genetic counseling of patients with Parkinson disease.
quotes: We suggest that testing for this mutation will be important in the management and genetic counselling of patients with Parkinson's disease.

notes.statement: Di Fonzo et al. (2005) found the heterozygous LRRK2 G2019S mutation in 4 of 61 (6.6%) unrelated families with autosomal dominant Parkinson disease, originating from Italy, Portugal, and Brazil, indicating its presence in different populations and identifying it as a common mutation in dominantly inherited Parkinson disease.
quotes: identified a heterozygous mutation (Gly2019 ser) present in four of 61 (6.6%) unrelated families with Parkinson's disease and autosomal dominant inheritance
identify a common mutation associated with dominantly inherited Parkinson's disease

notes.statement: Nichols et al. (2005) screened 767 affected individuals from 358 multiplex Parkinson disease families for the LRRK2 G2019S mutation. They found it in 35 individuals (5%): 34 heterozygotes and 1 homozygote. The authors concluded that this single mutation causes Parkinson disease in 5% of individuals with familial disease.
quotes: Of 767 affected individuals from 358 multiplex families, 35 (5%) individuals were either heterozygous (34) or homozygous (one) for the mutation
our results suggest that a single LRRK2 mutation causes Parkinson's disease in 5% of individuals with familial disease.

notes.statement: Nichols et al. (2005) recommended that screening for the LRRK2 G2019S mutation be a component of genetic testing for Parkinson disease.
quotes: Screening for this mutation should be a component of genetic testing for Parkinson's disease.

notes.statement: By high-resolution recombination mapping and candidate gene sequencing in 46 families with autosomal dominant, late-onset parkinsonism linked to chromosome 12p11.2-q13.1 (PARK8), Zimprich et al. (2004) identified 6 disease-segregating mutations (5 missense and 1 putative splice site mutation) in the LRRK2 gene.
quotes: We have previously linked families with autosomal-dominant, late-onset parkinsonism to chromosome 12p11.2-q13.1 (PARK8).

By high-resolution recombination mapping and candidate gene sequencing in 46 families, we have found six disease-segregating mutations (five missense and one putative splice site mutation) in a gene encoding a large, multifunctional protein, LRRK2 (leucine-rich repeat kinase 2).

notes.statement: Zimprich et al. (2004) found that 6 postmortem examinations of affected carriers in families A and D showed brainstem dopaminergic degeneration with diverse pathologies, including Lewy body Parkinson disease, diffuse Lewy body disease, nigral degeneration without distinctive histopathology, and progressive supranuclear palsy-like pathology. They suggested that LRRK2 may be central to the pathogenesis of several major neurodegenerative disorders associated with parkinsonism.
quotes: Within affected carriers of families A and D, six post mortem diagnoses reveal brainstem dopaminergic degeneration accompanied by strikingly diverse pathologies.
Hence, LRRK2 may be central to the pathogenesis of several major neurodegenerative disorders associated with parkinsonism.

notes.statement: Zimprich et al. (2004) noted that LRRK2 belongs to the ROCO protein family and contains a protein kinase domain of the MAPKKK class along with several other major functional domains.
quotes: It belongs to the ROCO protein family and includes a protein kinase domain of the MAPKKK class and several other major functional domains.

notes.statement: Paisán-Ruíz et al. (2004) named the PARK8 protein dardarin, from the Basque word dardara, meaning tremor, because of the tremor seen in PD and because several of the families were of Basque descent.
quotes: Because of the tremor observed in PD and because a number of the families are of Basque descent, we have named this protein dardarin, derived from the Basque word dardara, meaning tremor.

notes.statement: Paisán-Ruíz et al. (2004) cloned a novel gene in the PARK8 region. In five families from England and Spain with PARK8-linked Parkinson disease, they found missense mutations in this gene that segregated with the disease.
quotes: We describe here the cloning of a novel gene that contains missense mutations segregating with PARK8-linked PD in five families from England and Spain.

notes.statement: Wszolek et al. (2004) found that genetic studies in a kindred with autosomal dominant parkinsonism suggested linkage to the PARK8 locus on chromosome 12.
quotes: Genetic studies suggested linkage to the PARK8 locus on chromosome 12.

notes.statement: Wszolek et al. (2004) reported that autopsies of 4 affected members of a PARK8-linked parkinsonian kindred showed variable pathology: all had nigral neuronal loss and gliosis, but Lewy bodies were brainstem-limited in one case and diffuse in another, one had neurofibrillary tangles without Lewy bodies, and one had neither tangles nor Lewy bodies.
quotes: Lewy bodies (LB) limited to brainstem nuclei were detected in one case, diffuse LB in the second, neurofibrillary tangles (NFT) without LB in the third, and neither NFT nor LB in the fourth.

notes.statement: Zimprich et al. (2004) tested 21 white families with Parkinson disease compatible with autosomal dominant transmission (84 affected and 83 unaffected members) using 29 markers in the PARK8 region on chromosome 12. Under heterogeneity with an affecteds-only model, they obtained a maximum multipoint LOD score of 2.01 (P = 0.0047), with an estimated proportion of linked families of 0.32.
quotes: We tested 21 white families with Parkinson disease and an inheritance pattern compatible with autosomal dominant transmission for linkage in this region.

Under the assumption of heterogeneity and through use of an affecteds-only model, a maximum multipoint LOD score of 2.01 was achieved in the total sample, with an estimated proportion of families with linkage of 0.32.

notes.statement: Zimprich et al. (2004) found that 2 families, a German Canadian family (family A) and a family from western Nebraska (family D), showed significant linkage on their own, with a combined multipoint LOD score of 3.33 (affecteds-only) or 3.92 (penetrance-dependent model). The 1-LOD support interval put the most likely disease location between a CA repeat on genomic clone AC025253 (44.5 Mb) and marker D12S1701 (47.7 Mb).
quotes: When a penetrance-dependent model was calculated, the combined multipoint LOD score achieved was 3.92
the 1-LOD support interval suggests that the most likely disease location is between a CA repeat polymorphism on genomic clone AC025253 (44.5 Mb) and marker D12S1701 (47.7 Mb).

notes.statement: Zimprich et al. (2004) concluded that the PARK8 locus causes disease in a subset of white families with autosomal dominant parkinsonism, suggesting that it could be a more common locus.
quotes: Our data provide evidence that the PARK8 locus is responsible for the disease in a subset of families of white ancestry with autosomal dominant parkinsonism, suggesting that it could be a more common locus.

notes.statement: Funayama et al. (2002) ran a genomewide linkage analysis in a Japanese family with autosomal dominant parkinsonism. The highest two-point LOD score was 4.32 at D12S345 (12p11.21), and multipoint analysis gave a maximum LOD of 4.71 at D12S85 (12q12). Haplotype analysis placed the disease-associated haplotype in a 13.6-cM interval in 12p11.2-q13.1, bounded by recombinations at D12S1631 and D12S339.
quotes: Parametric two-point linkage analysis yielded a highest log odds (LOD) score of 4.32 at D12S345 (12p11.21).
Parametric multipoint linkage analysis of the 13.6cM interval around this marker yielded LOD scores almost uniformly of >4.0 with a Z(max) of 4.71 at D12S85 (12q12).
Haplotype analysis detected two obligate recombination events at D12S1631 and D12S339 and defined the disease-associated haplotype in the 13.6cM interval in 12p11.2-q13.1.

notes.statement: Funayama et al. (2002) also ran nonparametric (penetrance-independent) linkage analyses, which gave maximum LOD scores of 14.2 (two-point) and 24.9 (multipoint) at D12S345. These results supported mapping the locus to 12p11.23-q13.11, a region different from any known hereditary parkinsonism locus. The new locus was named PARK8.
quotes: Nonparametric two-point and multipoint linkage analyses, which are penetrance-independent, yielded Z(max) LOD scores of 14.2 and 24.9 at D12S345, respectively, strongly supporting the mapping of the parkinsonism locus in this family to 12p11.23-q13.11.
The nomenclature of PARK8 was assigned to the new locus.

notes.statement: Funayama et al. (2002) found that some unaffected family members carried the disease haplotype, which suggested incomplete penetrance. They proposed that environmental or other genetic factors modify expression of the disease.
quotes: This haplotype was shared by all the patients and by some unaffected carriers, suggesting that disease penetration in this family is incomplete.
This low penetrance suggests that environmental or other genetic factors modify expression of the disease.

notes.statement: Hasegawa and Kowa (1997) reported that although the clinical features of the Sagamihara family with autosomal dominant Parkinson disease did not differ from common PD, autopsied cases showed only mild to moderate loss of melanin-containing cells, preserved locus ceruleus neurons, and no Lewy bodies.
quotes: Clinical features of this family did not differ from common PD, however, neuropathological findings were different from PD.
No Lewy bodies were detected at all from any region where Lewy bodies frequently appear in PD.

notes.statement: Wszolek et al. (1995) described family D, a 6-generation western Nebraska kindred of probable English ancestry with 18 affected members among 188 individuals, showing autosomal dominant, slowly progressive, levodopa-responsive parkinsonism. They concluded that the disorder closely resembled, if not identical to, idiopathic Parkinson disease.
quotes: We studied a family (family D) whose ancestors probably immigrated to the United States from England.
This large kindred appears to represent a neurodegenerative disorder closely resembling, if not identical to, idiopathic PD.

notes.statement: In family D, Wszolek et al. (1995) found that [18F]-6-fluoro-L-dopa PET in 1 affected individual showed decreased uptake in a pattern consistent with PD. Autopsy of another affected individual showed neuronal and pigment loss, gliosis, and Lewy bodies in the substantia nigra pars compacta.
quotes: PET with [18F]-6-fluoro-L-dopa (FD) performed on an affected individual revealed decreased uptake of FD in a pattern consistent with PD.
Autopsy performed on another affected individual demonstrated neuronal and pigmentary loss, gliosis, and Lewy bodies in the substantia nigra pars compacta.
